content: Motivational interviewing's elicit-provide-elicit: ask what the person already knows/thinks, ask permission before offering information/advice, then elicit their reaction. Asking permission signals respect for autonomy and avoids the righting reflex/lecturing that produces resistance. Well-established clinical technique (decades of MI literature, strong practitioner consensus), though most evidence is from clinical/health-behavior counseling contexts rather than consumer chatbot contexts.
